habitat: Grass and coarse vegetation fringing marshes, riverine reed beds and papyrus, cultivated fields, fallow lands and cane fields. In summer the male flies over his territory.
summary: A common resident. The red shoulder is retained all year. The breeding male is identified by a pale bill and a short tail, as well as the red shoulders. The display call is a husky tseek, wirra, wirra, wirra, wirra. The female and non-breeding plumage, apart from the red shoulder, were not described. The only grade A recordings are ND, so the playable recording is grade B. The Kemp paper name Redshouldered Widow and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: White-winged Widowbird has a yellow-and-white shoulder and a broad tail. Fan-tailed Widowbird has a red shoulder and a short tail.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The female was not described. The red shoulder is kept all year, and the pale bill and short tail identify the breeding male. The grade A calls are ND, so the playable file is grade B and its filename includes a Cape Canary. No flight photograph was found. Population figures and the Kemp name Redshouldered Widow were left unchanged.
